segments.text: Next vnto the place of the image of god, is adioyned the place of the firſt ſinne. For ſeeing man was created to the imade of God, that is, perfectly wiſe, perfectly righteous, & perfectly bleſſed, the queſtiō hath been not without cauſe in all times, whence this preſent eſtate of man commeth, wherein he, except he be born again by the holy ghoſt, cannot do other than ſin, and be obnoxious to calamities of all ſortes, and at length to death it ſelfe. To this queſtion anſwere cannot be made but out of the doctrine of the Church onely: which is, that all this confuſion and miſerie floweth from the firſt ſinne of our firſt Parents. We muſt ſee therefore what that ſinne is: concerning which, fower thinges eſpecially come to bee conſidered.

1 What it was.
2 What the cauſes thereof.
3 What the effectes.
4 Why god permitted it.
